findings.statement: NNMT expression is associated with earlier progression in the CheckMate-025 nivolumab, everolimus and Choueiri 2016 arms, but none of these differences is significant, and the nivolumab vs everolimus difference has a non-significant adjusted p-value [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]. It is a lead, not a predictor, and the Choueiri arm is small.

CA9 is associated with longer benefit on the IMmotion150 combination, atezolizumab and sunitinib arms, but the difference between the combination and sunitinib has a non-significant adjusted p-value [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. CA9 is therefore not a treatment-selection biomarker in this data.

Higher PSAT1 is associated with earlier progression in atezolizumab, both CheckMate-025 arms and the small Choueiri nivolumab trial, with no significant arm difference (nivolumab vs everolimus adjusted p-value) [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]. Its biomarker value rests on tumour-vs-normal change and prognosis, not on drug-response data.

PSAT1 is lower in tumours but higher in BAP1-mutant ones in TCGA RNA, with a positive mutant minus wild-type difference [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711]. The tool does not flag it as a subgroup target candidate because the CPTAC protein difference is not significant, and it is also higher in ccB.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is lower in ccB than ccA in TCGA RNA, and the tool marks it as defining the ccA/ccB split [gene=EPAS1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-0.935]. No mutation-defined subgroup is flagged, and the CPTAC protein difference between ccB and ccA is not significant.

NNMT is not a subgroup target candidate: none of the VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 comparisons is significant, including the VHL TCGA RNA adjusted p-value [gene=NNMT; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; VHL.tcga_rna.padj=0.141]. Its tumour increase therefore looks pan-subtype and not tied to one genotype.

CA9 has a surface call, a known-target flag and high vital-organ staining in stomach, plus vital-organ protein enrichment, a safety concern. In the weakest quarter of donors only a minority of tumour cells express it [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%]. CSPA did not observe it at the surface, and a high score does not show a conjugate would work.

CD70 has a surface call, no vital-organ proteome enrichment and one of the top suitability ranks [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]. Human Protein Atlas staining data are not available for it, so normal-tissue safety is only partly assessed.

ENPP3 is a known target with CSPA high-confidence surface observation, but kidney staining is at the maximum level [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0], and duodenum staining is also at the maximum level. The weak tumour-vs-normal contrast and the on-target kidney exposure argue for caution.

SCARB1 is the top-ranked target-profile gene and is observed at the surface by CSPA, but it is enriched in a vital organ (adrenal gland), with a high tissue-specificity score [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.08]. This is an on-target, off-tumour safety concern for a conjugate or radioligand, and it is not a known ADC target.

Immune cells make most of the CD70 tumour transcripts [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]. It correlates positively with CD8 and regulatory T cells and has a negative log hazard ratio on atezolizumab + bevacizumab, so CD70 may be as much an immune-axis target as a tumour-cell one.

FCGR3A tracks the immune score closely across tumours (Spearman rho) [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.795]. Its tumour increase reflects infiltration, not tumour-cell expression, so it is an immune-infiltration marker and not a tumour-cell target.

Immune cells make most of the SLC16A3 tumour transcripts [gene=SLC16A3; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.667], although its CD8 T-cell correlation is near zero. This conflicts with the high purity-robust tumour-intrinsic score in the ranking, so its cell attribution needs a direct single-cell check.

The cell attribution of SCARB1 does not replicate: the dominant group is Myeloid in Li 2022 and RCC in Zhang 2021, and its tumour-cell share in Li 2022 is a minority [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336]. The tumour-vs-tubule fold change is positive in both datasets, but Zhang 2021 has only a few paired donors.

NNMT is called RCC (tumour cell) in both single-cell datasets, with a high Zhang 2021 tumour-cell share [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948]. This supports a tumour-intrinsic origin, with the caveat of only seven donors and a few paired donors.

CA9 is called RCC in both single-cell datasets, and the Zhang 2021 tumour vs proximal tubule log2 fold change is strongly positive [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=8.522]. The tumour-cell attribution is therefore consistent across datasets.

The SCARB1 protein increase replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort, with a positive log2 fold change [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334]. Direction and significance agree with the discovery cohort.

The PSAT1 protein decrease replicates in the confirmatory cohort, with a negative log2 fold change [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]. The one phosphosite measured in both cohorts did not replicate.

The NNMT protein increase replicates in the confirmatory cohort, with a positive log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]. The fold change is larger than in discovery, which is expected with a different technology and does not by itself indicate stronger biology.

caveats: No gene differs between trial arms after correction in IMmotion150 or CheckMate 025; all treatment findings are associations, not predictions, and the Choueiri 2016 arm has only 16 patients.
CA9 was not tested in the confirmatory cohort (absent or too sparse there); this is not a failure to replicate. CD70 has no Human Protein Atlas staining data.
ADC suitability scores do not show a conjugate or radioligand would work. SCARB1 and CA9 are enriched in vital organs, ENPP3 stains strongly in kidney.
PCK1, SLC16A3 (subtype, ADC and confirmatory layers), EPAS1 and other ranked genes (ALDH6A1, SLC6A19, PPP1R1A) were not profiled in every layer within the call budget.
The single-cell replication uses only a few paired donors in Zhang 2021; the immune-cell share of SLC16A3 conflicts with its tumour-intrinsic rank and was not resolved.
Convergence ranks (target: SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT; biomarker: PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, SLC6A19, PPP1R1A) come from the integration script and are not independent validation.
